description: Reads one graph you saved earlier, by its graph_id, and returns the whole model in the same shape the run tools accept. Use this when you want to show the user what is in a saved model, edit it before running it again, or run it with run_monte_carlo_simulation, which takes the model inline and not a graph_id. To find a graph_id first, call list_graphs. It returns the graph_id, the name, when it was last updated, and the graph itself: its uncertain inputs with their distributions, the formula nodes, the links between them and the run settings. It reads the model, not any result of running it. It needs a Neumann account: send your key, or your signed-in token, in the Authorization header as a Bearer credential. No Neumann tool takes an api_key argument. Cost: free -- it debits no credits and spends none of your free daily runs -- but it needs an account; an anonymous caller gets authentication_required.

graph_id.description: Which saved graph to read, from save_graph or list_graphs.
graph_id.title: Graph Id

AggregationRequest.description:
A post-simulation, series-aware metric over one node's full series.

NPV/IRR/payback/CAGR/cumsum are NOT per-period node values: they consume a
target node's complete ``(time_periods x trials)`` matrix AFTER the run and
return one value per trial, summarised into a distribution.

Discount convention (0-based series index): period ``t=0`` is the present
(undiscounted) cash flow; period ``t`` is discounted by ``(1+rate)**t``. The
first period is undiscounted.

Warning — two discount conventions coexist; do not mix them. These
aggregations use the **0-based** series index above (first period
undiscounted). The per-period formula functions ``DISCOUNT(rate,
{time_period})`` and ``PV(rate, value, {time_period})`` use the **1-based**
``{time_period}``, so they discount the first period by ``(1+rate)**1``.

"Investment at period 0" pattern: model an up-front outlay as a negative
period-0 cash flow in the target node's series; NPV's t=0-undiscounted
convention then treats it as the present-value outlay. Do not additionally
discount that first period with ``PV(...,{time_period})`` inside the target
node's formula when also requesting an aggregation ``npv`` — combining the
1-based per-period discount with the 0-based ``npv`` double-shifts the first
period.

Per-period node vs aggregate metric (``prob``): pointing ``prob`` at a
multi-period cash-flow NODE via ``target_node_id`` thresholds only that node's
FINAL-period per-trial value — i.e. ``P(per-period value > x)``, NOT
``P(NPV > x)``. To get a true ``P(NPV > 0)``, define an ``npv`` aggregation
first, then add a ``prob`` aggregation whose ``target_aggregation_id`` points
at that ``npv`` id; ``prob`` then thresholds the NPV per-trial vector directly.
A ``prob`` request targets EITHER a node (``target_node_id``) OR an earlier
aggregation (``target_aggregation_id``) — exactly one, never both.

function.description: One of: npv, irr, payback, discounted_payback, cagr, cumsum, prob, terminal_value, mirr. discounted_payback requires params.rate; npv requires params.rate OR a per-period params.rates curve; prob requires params.op (one of >, >=, <, <=, ==) and params.value; terminal_value requires params.g and params.rate; mirr requires params.finance_rate and params.reinvest_rate.
function.title: Function

id.description: Result key for this metric (unique within the request).
id.title: Id

params.description: Function params, e.g. {'rate': 0.1} for npv/discounted_payback, {'op': '>', 'value': 0} for prob, {'g': 0.02, 'rate': 0.1} for terminal_value, {'finance_rate': 0.1, 'reinvest_rate': 0.08} for mirr.
params.title: Params

target_aggregation_id.description: For a ``prob`` request only: the id of an aggregation defined EARLIER in this output_request whose per-trial vector (e.g. an ``npv``) is thresholded. Lets ``P(NPV > 0)`` be expressed directly instead of the per-period ``P(value > x)`` you get by targeting a multi-period node. The referenced aggregation must produce a per-trial vector (npv/irr/payback/discounted_payback/cagr/cumsum/terminal_value/mirr).
target_aggregation_id.title: Target Aggregation Id

target_node_id.description: The node whose full per-period series the metric consumes. Required for every metric except a ``prob`` that targets a prior aggregation via ``target_aggregation_id``. Exactly one of ``target_node_id`` / ``target_aggregation_id`` may be set on a ``prob`` request.
target_node_id.title: Target Node Id

CalcNode.description:
A computed node. ``formula`` is OPTIONAL.

A null/empty/whitespace formula is allowed: the node is treated as a
constant ``0`` every period/trial (incoming edges are ignored — there is no
implicit "sum of incoming edges"). ``check_simulation_model`` surfaces this as a
WARNING, not an error. To sum incoming edges, write the sum explicitly,
e.g. ``{e1}+{e2}``; for pass-through use ``{e1}``.

formula.description: Optional expression over incoming edge ids, e.g. '{e1} * 0.5 + {e2}'. To sum incoming edges write '{e1}+{e2}'; for pass-through use '{e1}'. If omitted/empty the node is treated as a constant 0 (sum-of-incoming is not implied); check_simulation_model reports this as a warning.
formula.title: Formula

id.description: Unique node id within the graph.
id.title: Id

RootNode.description:
A source node that samples from a probability distribution each period.

``json_schema_extra`` (neumann#288) attaches a ``oneOf`` discriminated on
``distribution_type``, so the published schema states each type's own
required ``distribution_params`` keys instead of advertising an opaque
object. The RUNTIME annotation stays ``dict[str, object]`` — see
``contracts.catalog.add_distribution_variants`` for why a real pydantic
discriminated union is not used here.
